content_preview.title: Modular Makes the MAX Source Available Under a New License That Bars Using It as Input to AI Reimplementations
content_preview.summary: Modular published the MAX graph compiler, runtime and hardware backends under a new MAX License that restricts AI-assisted reimplementation and distribution of modified source, while Apache 2.0 parts stay.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Modular announced on October 22, 2026 that [the complete MAX source code is now publicly available](https://www.modular.com/blog/max-license), released alongside a new MAX License. The company's post describes the newly opened pieces, the graph compiler, runtime and hardware backends for CPUs and GPUs, as "source available". The license text, last modified October 21, 2026, names the licensor as Modular Inc, [a Qualcomm Company](https://github.com/modular/modular/blob/main/Licenses/...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well structured News piece (939 words, range 400-1200). Separates the vendor's announcement from the license text, quotes the AI clause in full including its carve-out for using AI tools to read, analyze, improve or explain MAX and to build software that interoperates with it, and gives the vendor's rationale in its own words.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read (decompressed, tags stripped, raw text): source-0 (modular.com/blog/max-license, 200): dated October 22, 2026; 'the complete MAX source code is now publicly available'; 'the graph compiler, runtime, and hardware backends. These include support for CPUs and GPUs'; timeline (Mojo stdlib 2024, kernels/models/serving/APIs 2025, Mojo compiler August); Apache 2.0 list and 'will remain under Apache 2.0'; three limitations with the exact quoted wording ('You can't use any part of MAX as input to an AI system to produce a reimplementation of MAX.', 'You can't publish or distribute modified MAX source code, except by forking MAX for the purpose of contributing changes back to the main project.', Modular Accelerated wordmark); rationale quotes; alliance program, 'a voice in governance and conformance standards', 'more permissive licensing'; Nov 10 10 AM PT Q&A with Chris Lattner and Tim Davis. All confirmed. source-1 (MAX_LICENSE on GitHub, 200): 'Last Modified: October 21, 2026'; 'Modular Inc, a Qualcomm Company'; s1.1 grant (perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free; reproduce and prepare Derivative Works; distribute in object code form); s1.1.2 downstream licensing, any portion of MAX stays subject to Terms; s1.3 fork exception ('to contribute to a Modular project'); s1.4(d) verbatim: 'You shall not use MAX, or any portion of it, as training data, fine-tuning data, or input to any AI system in order to produce software that reimplements or substitutes for MAX, whether or not it contains literal copies of MAX. This does not restrict using AI tools to read, analyze, improve, or explain MAX, or to develop Your own software that runs on or interoperates with MAX.' (article quotes both parts exactly); s1.5 Apache components; s2.1 usage data 'for any purpose' and Modular owns it; s3.3 hosted/managed service by a legal entity, written approval of materials bearing the Marks. All confirmed. Live re-fetch of raw.githubusercontent MAX_LICENSE matched clause 1.4(d) and dates. source-2 (github.com/modular/modular README, 200): 'Portions of the MAX source code and its binary distribution are licensed under the Licenses/MAX_LICENSE, with the remainder of the source under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions' confirmed. source-3 (opensource.org/osd): snapshot came from Archive.org fallback but live page (re-fetched, 200) has identical text, 'Last modified on February 16, 2024'. Every OSD quote verified word for word: 'Open source doesn't just mean access to the source code.' (source uses a curly apostrophe; article uses a straight one, typographic only); criterion 4 quote is a single contiguous quotation, exact including curly quotes around 'patch files' (the writer-flagged split no longer exists in the submitted text and the automated mismatch is not reproduced); criterion 6 quote exact. The OSD section is purely factual: it states that the Herald found no OSI assessment of the MAX License and that Modular itself uses 'source available'; it does not say the license fails or meets the OSD. Independent-source note: the OSD is the only non-vendor source and is used for reference only; the article makes no claim that depends on independent coverage. suspicious_patterns: null for all four sources. Allowlist: modular.com, github.com and opensource.org each present by exact hostname (config/source_allowlist.txt lines 220, 1131, 2430); the www.modular.com host passed the script's allowlist check.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every statement about what the license permits or bars traces to the license text or Modular's post and is not stated more strongly than either. Title check: 'Bars Using It as Input to AI Reimplementations' matches clause 1.4(d), which bars use as training data, fine-tuning data or input to an AI system to produce software that reimplements or substitutes for MAX; the title is slightly narrower than the clause (it omits training data and 'substitutes for') but not misleading, and the body quotes the full clause with its carve-out. The post and license differ slightly on modified source (post: fork to contribute back; license s1.3: fork of Modular's official repository to contribute to a Modular project) and the article presents both. The article does not call the license open source or not open source. Cross-link /article/2026-08/18-modular-open-sources-the-mojo-compiler-under-apache-20-ending-a-four-year-closed-compiler-era exists in src/content/articles and is described accurately (compiler release). Orphan-link check: all four body URLs are in article.sources; the only other link is the internal article path.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Vendor claims attributed to the vendor ('Modular says', 'The post states'); no loaded language about Modular. Defamation care applied: no characterisation of Modular's motives beyond quoted statements.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Related prior Herald coverage is the August Mojo compiler open-sourcing article, linked in the body and in article-meta as a related article. No duplicate of the other recent Modular items.
concerns: Automated 'AI self-reference' warning (pattern \bas an ai\b) is a false positive: it matches 'as an AI-produced reimplementation of MAX' in the 'What We Don't Know' section, which describes how Modular would classify a project, not the author. Overridden to APPROVE after reading it in context.

The article says the reviewed sources contain no independent legal analysis of the license rather than stating outright that no independent coverage was found; this is accurate and non-misleading but slightly less explicit than ideal.
recommendations: For future license stories, state explicitly that no independent coverage or legal commentary was located, and consider quoting the license's 'whether or not it contains literal copies of MAX' language.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully sourced and neutral coverage of a license change; ready for publication with no corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate license story of interest to developers of AI infrastructure, but narrow in audience and no independent confirmation
